html:
The Miriwoong are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country around present-day Kununurra and the lower Ord River in the east Kimberley, with the small Doolboong group on the coast to the north. The map shows them together from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Gajirrawoong on the coast, the Ngarinyman and Jaminjung to the east and the Kija to the south. Cattle stations took their land from the 1880s.

The 20th century changed the land itself. The Ord River irrigation scheme built Kununurra in the 1960s, and the Ord River Dam, finished in the early 1970s, flooded a large part of Miriwoong country under Lake Argyle. The Argyle diamond mine worked nearby from 1985 to 2020. The Miriwoong language now has few fluent speakers, and a language centre in Kununurra works to teach it.
